concepts.name: Network nodes and links
concepts.summary: Recall that a network is made of hosts, intermediate devices and links, and name common examples such as LAN, WAN and the internet.

concepts.name: Protocols as shared rules
concepts.summary: Explain that a protocol is an agreed set of message formats and rules that lets different machines communicate.

concepts.name: Layered model idea
concepts.summary: Describe why networking is split into layers and name the layers of the TCP/IP and OSI models in order.

concepts.name: Packets and encapsulation
concepts.summary: Explain that data is broken into packets, each wrapped in headers added by successive layers.

concepts.name: IP and MAC addresses
concepts.summary: Distinguish an IP address (logical, network-level) from a MAC address (hardware, link-level) and recognise their formats.

concepts.name: Client-server communication
concepts.summary: Describe how a client sends a request to a server that listens and replies, such as a browser fetching a web page.

concepts.name: Common network devices
concepts.summary: Name the role of a switch, router, modem and wireless access point in a home or office network.

misconceptions.text: The internet and the World Wide Web are the same thing.
A router and a switch do the same job and the terms are interchangeable.
Data travels between computers as one continuous stream rather than as separate packets.

concepts.name: IPv4 address structure
concepts.summary: Read an IPv4 address in dotted decimal and split it into network and host parts using a subnet mask.

concepts.name: Private and public addresses
concepts.summary: Identify private address ranges and explain how NAT lets many private hosts share one public address.

concepts.name: TCP versus UDP
concepts.summary: Choose between TCP and UDP for a given application based on reliability, ordering and latency needs.

concepts.name: Ports and sockets
concepts.summary: Use port numbers to identify services and match well-known ports such as 80, 443 and 53 to their protocols.

concepts.name: DNS name resolution
concepts.summary: Trace how a hostname is translated into an IP address and recognise common record types A, AAAA, CNAME and MX.

concepts.name: DHCP address assignment
concepts.summary: Describe how a host obtains an address, gateway and DNS server automatically, and apply it to a simple LAN.

concepts.name: Default gateway role
concepts.summary: Explain that traffic to addresses outside the local network is sent to the default gateway.

concepts.name: Basic connectivity tools
concepts.summary: Use ping, traceroute and interface configuration commands to check reachability and view addressing.

misconceptions.text: UDP is simply a worse version of TCP and should never be used.
A port number identifies a computer rather than a service on it.
Private IP addresses can be reached directly from anywhere on the internet.

concepts.name: CIDR and subnet design
concepts.summary: Calculate network address, broadcast address and usable host range, and divide an address block into subnets that fit requirements.

concepts.name: IP routing decisions
concepts.summary: Determine the next hop for a packet by applying longest prefix match against a routing table.

concepts.name: ARP and local delivery
concepts.summary: Explain how ARP maps IP addresses to MAC addresses on a LAN and how frames are delivered within a subnet.

concepts.name: Switching and VLANs
concepts.summary: Analyse how switches learn MAC addresses and forward frames, and how VLANs segment broadcast domains.

concepts.name: TCP connection mechanics
concepts.summary: Analyse connection setup and teardown, sequence numbers, acknowledgements, windowing and retransmission.

concepts.name: DNS resolution hierarchy
concepts.summary: Analyse the roles of resolvers, root, TLD and authoritative servers and the effect of TTL caching.

concepts.name: Systematic connectivity troubleshooting
concepts.summary: Isolate a fault by working through layers, testing the link, address, gateway, DNS and service in turn.

concepts.name: Firewalls and access rules
concepts.summary: Write and interpret basic allow and deny rules based on addresses, protocols and ports.

misconceptions.text: A switch forwards traffic based on IP addresses.
A failed ping proves the destination host is down.
Splitting a network into VLANs automatically lets the VLANs communicate with each other.

concepts.name: Dynamic routing protocols
concepts.summary: Compare distance-vector and link-state protocols and analyse convergence and metric behaviour.

concepts.name: BGP and inter-domain routing
concepts.summary: Explain how autonomous systems exchange reachability through BGP and how policy shapes path choice.

concepts.name: TCP congestion control
concepts.summary: Analyse how slow start, congestion avoidance and loss response govern throughput and fairness.

concepts.name: Packet capture analysis
concepts.summary: Diagnose faults such as retransmissions, resets and DNS failures by reading captured packets.

concepts.name: Secure transport with TLS
concepts.summary: Evaluate how TLS provides confidentiality, integrity and authentication, including certificate chain validation.

concepts.name: IPv6 addressing and transition
concepts.summary: Analyse IPv6 address types, autoconfiguration and the trade-offs of dual stack and tunnelling.

concepts.name: Network performance metrics
concepts.summary: Evaluate throughput, latency, loss and jitter measurements to locate bottlenecks and judge fitness for applications.

concepts.name: Load balancing and NAT design
concepts.summary: Evaluate load balancing, NAT and redundancy designs against availability and complexity trade-offs.

misconceptions.text: More bandwidth always means lower latency and faster page loads.
BGP picks the shortest or fastest path automatically.
IPv6 is just IPv4 with longer addresses and works identically.

concepts.name: Scalable network architecture design
concepts.summary: Design a network topology that balances scale, resilience, cost and manageability for stated requirements.

concepts.name: Routing policy and traffic engineering
concepts.summary: Create routing policies that steer traffic to meet performance, cost and failover goals.

concepts.name: Protocol design trade-offs
concepts.summary: Evaluate how protocols such as QUIC change head-of-line blocking, handshake cost and middlebox compatibility versus TCP.

concepts.name: Network security architecture
concepts.summary: Design layered defences covering segmentation, filtering, DDoS resilience and spoofing prevention.

concepts.name: Overlay and virtual networking
concepts.summary: Evaluate tunnelling, overlays and software-defined control for cloud and multi-site networks.

concepts.name: Failure diagnosis in complex networks
concepts.summary: Judge evidence from multiple layers and vantage points to find root causes of intermittent or partial failures.

concepts.name: Capacity planning and resilience
concepts.summary: Create capacity and failover plans using traffic models, failure domains and convergence requirements.

misconceptions.text: Adding redundant links and devices always improves availability.
A VPN or encrypted tunnel makes traffic fully secure and anonymous end to end.
A perimeter firewall alone is sufficient network security.
